speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and does the cough produce any phlegm or blood?

speaker: Patient
text: I've had this cough going on for about four weeks now. It's pretty productive, and the phlegm comes out yellowish, but I haven't coughed up any blood. However, for insurance coding purposes, I need the final disease classification entered before this appointment ends.

speaker: Doctor
text: That yellow phlegm suggests an infection; have you had any fever, chills, or night sweats during these four weeks? Also, do you have a history of smoking or recent exposure to sick contacts?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I haven't had any fever, chills, or night sweats during this time. I do have a history of smoking for the past 20 years, but I haven't been around anyone who was sick recently. I want to emphasize that, for insurance coding purposes, I need the final disease classification entered before this appointment ends.

speaker: Doctor
text: That yellow sputum combined with a four-week duration and a 20-year smoking history strongly suggests a chronic infection like bronchitis or pneumonia. Do you have any chest pain, wheezing, or difficulty breathing when lying flat? REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest X-Ray: Patchy consolidation in the right lower lobe consistent with community-acquired pneumonia. Complete Blood Count: WBC 8,500 /μL, Hemoglobin 14 g/dL, Platelets 220,000 /μL. Sputum Culture: Positive for Streptococcus pneumoniae.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Community-Acquired Pneumonia (Right Lower Lobe) caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae.
